The subject stands slightly right of center, with the distant end of the background faintly revealing the cool morning light of the stadium. Depth of field is moderate to ensure both the person and the practice sword are clearly visible. Soft natural light enters from the side of the tunnel, preserving realistic shadow layers on the face and wrists, while occasional side light creates brief glints along the edge of the sword. Her sleeve and hair strands show slight movement. The starting motion is controlled, with muscle force transmitted sequentially through the shoulder, elbow, and wrist.

The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one to the trackside, using a low-angle, eye-level tracking shot that transitions from wide to medium. The red curved track and grass edge form horizontal leading lines. The subject enters from the left side of the frame, with the background showing the empty morning stands and sky not yet fully bright. The space is more open, allowing full release of the action’s explosive power. Lighting remains primarily natural, but side lighting more distinctly outlines the blade and outer arm contours, clearly capturing the movement of the hem and footfalls. She first steps forward to complete the advance, then performs cloud hands with the sword, rotating her wrist in a circular motion, drawing a smooth arc along the outer side of her body axis. Next, she spins and slashes downward, lowering her center of gravity and tapping the ground at the lowest point to leverage momentum, then quickly taps again and flicks upward. The kinetic chain transfers from ankle, knee, hip, through the shoulder and arm to the sword tip—explosive yet controlled. The hem and ends of her hair swing naturally with the spin, showing delayed motion. The camera initially tracks horizontally to keep her centered, then makes a small circular movement during the spin, tilts slightly down during the slash to follow the blade's descent, and quickly pulls back to a medium shot during the flick-up, enhancing speed and spatial displacement. The overall atmosphere remains quiet and concentrated.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, wide-angle high-angle composition overlooking the entire rain-soaked rooftop court from above. Focus shifts from glowing hoop to the central confrontation between the smiling hamburger and angry apple. Raindrops glisten on the hamburger bun, and the apple's top leaf trembles slightly in the wind. The camera slowly descends and pushes forward.

Shot 2 hard-cut transition from previous shot, medium-close eye-level slightly low angle tracking from the hamburger’s ball-handling side. Composition creates a sense of depth with the foreground basketball and blurred defender in the background. Wet court lines form leading lines toward the basket. Cool overhead lights and billboard side-backlight highlight the hamburger’s rounded edges. The smiling hamburger quickly lowers its center of gravity and dribbles aggressively forward. Lettuce edges and sesame seeds on the bun vibrate slightly with motion.

Shot 3 hard cut from previous shot, medium eye-level front-side composition, focus shifts to the angry apple. Foreground shows the apple’s outstretched defensive silhouette, background shows the hamburger still probing. Billboard lights in the rain fog are compressed into shallow depth-of-field bokeh. Shoes slide rapidly on wet ground, leaving semi-circular water trails. Hamburger shoulders shift left and right in feinting motion. Muffled Chinese gasps emerge from the crowd. Camera performs short lateral move to maintain full confrontation space.

Shot 4 hard cut with accelerated pacing from previous shot, close-up low-angle oblique side shot. Basketball placed at lower golden ratio point. Hamburger and apple occupy left and right sides, creating head-on tension. Neon light casts diagonal reflections on wet ground, enhancing speed. Core moment: hamburger suddenly executes a between-the-legs crossover, ball passing under body to opposite hand, shifting weight instantly. Apple’s defensive step is momentarily thrown off by half a step, top leaf flung sideways. Ball trajectory is clear and continuous, ingredients’ fabric-like edges flutter. Camera rapidly zooms in slightly with minor pan, synchronizing dribble

Shot 5 hard cut from previous shot, wide eye-level slightly rear-side tracking. Uses sideline and backboard support as strong leading lines. Foreground shows apple hastily turning back, focus locked on hamburger already completing spin. Background hoop grows larger through rain and purple-blue light strips. Main lighting remains from overhead and billboard reflections. Hamburger uses half-step advantage to spin and drive to basket, body angling inward. Apple slides in pursuit but distance increases. Water splashes are repeatedly shattered underfoot. Camera performs lateral pan followed by forward tracking, fully capturing the driving displacement.

Shot 6 hard cut into climax from previous shot, close-up upward angle focusing on upper body and ball-handling hand of hamburger. Shallow depth-of-field blurs hoop and signboards into dazzling neon bokeh. Cold backlight highlights water droplets on hamburger’s outline. Fine texture of bun surface, tense lips, and forceful upward hand motion become absolute focal points. Hamburger stops abruptly under basket, leans back, raises ball-handling arm swiftly to shoot, other hand maintains balance. Expression shifts from focus to determination. At ball release, water droplets are flung outward forming brief arcs.

Shot 7 hard cut from previous shot, close-up upward angle targeting hoop and incoming ball trajectory. Foreground features slightly trembling net, midground shows spinning approaching ball, background displays suddenly brightened high-rise signs and neon sky. Lighting maintains cool blue-purple tone but brightness sharply increases at scoring moment. Ball grazes net edge and goes in, white net ropes flip downward. Electronic signboard flashes brightly, wet metal frame reflects sharp highlights. Net

Shot 8 hard cut from previous shot, medium high-angle slightly oblique shot locking onto angry apple. Foreground shows extended arm sweeping across frame, background shows hamburger already landed and turning back, slightly blurred. Ground reflection emphasizes apple’s unbalanced path. Apple’s expression shifts from firmness to shock—eyes wide, body still sliding in momentum but completely missing. Foot drags long water trail. Top leaf and surface droplets violently swing due to sudden stop. Camera performs brief downward follow.

Wide eye-level slightly upward composition places characters centrally at bottom of frame. Foreground shows basketball still spinning on hamburger’s fingertip. Midground features court wrapped in neon rain mist and faint steam. Background shows layered city skyline and blinking billboards. Cool blue-purple tone remains consistent. Overhead lights and billboard reflections create soft rim light around hamburger. Camera slowly pulls back and slightly rises, capturing both outcome and high-altitude urban atmosphere. Chinese cheers spread and gradually recede, leaving only night wind, distant scoreboard echo, and faint humming of spinning ball. Final fade-out ends on city skyline.

Cool lighting evenly suppresses depth. Manes are lifted by strong wind as both lions lower their bodies and slowly advance. Wind Camera slowly descends and slightly pushes in.

Shot 2 connects with the previous shot via hard cut, medium eye-level lateral pan focusing on the circling paths of the two lions. Scattered tires and tilted car doors in foreground and background create spatial depth. They circle cautiously, shoulders rising and falling, front paws raised in defensive and aggressive stances. Paws step on gravel, kicking up brief dust clouds. Cold wind continues throughout the soundscape.

Shot 3 connects with the previous shot via rapid hard cut, close-up high-angle shot magnifying the head and forepaws of one lion in the foreground, while the other approaches from behind and to the side in shallow depth of field. Headwind causes the mane to glow with sharp edge highlights. The main subject does not throw a direct punch but lunges forward aggressively, forepaws sweeping past the lens. Mane, saliva, and sand explode into the air. A deep roar intensifies at this moment. Camera briefly tilts back to simulate impact.

Shot 4 connects with the previous shot via match-on-action cut, close-up side view. One lion suddenly shifts sideways into a low stance, twisting shoulder and torso to generate force. The other quickly tucks in and retreats to avoid frontal collision. The frame uses a broken car frame for horizontal obstruction, keeping focus tightly on the narrow gap between their bodies. Under cool natural light, muscle definition and airborne dust particles are clearly visible. Camera follows laterally in short distance.

Shot 5 connects with the previous shot via hard cut, overhead medium-close shot revealing terrain danger. One lion, retreating rapidly, crashes into the edge of a wrecked car, slipping on the sloped metal and sand layer. The car door vibrates, producing a hollow metallic echo. The other stops two steps away, lowering its body to prepare. The shattered window creates a framing device, placing the pressured lion below to enhance instability. Wind is amplified by vehicle resonance. Camera makes a slight dive then stops.

Shot 6 connects with the previous shot via brief dust cloud transition, follow shot from side-rear medium view. The slipping lion quickly regains balance, drives forward with front limbs, not delivering a damaging strike but launching a powerful frontal approach and shoulder charge. The other simultaneously sidesteps to evade. Dust trails form clear motion paths. Backlight turns airborne particles into silvery-gray specks. Camera rapidly pushes forward then slightly sways right.

Shot 7 connects with the previous shot via hard cut, close-up eye-level shot capturing the moment the two lions pass closely. One lifts its head in an upward threatening gesture, nostrils flaring, eyes sharp. The other pauses briefly at extreme proximity, then blinks to avoid contact. Shallow depth of field blurs the background ruins into cold indistinct patches. Backlight only outlines mane edges and whiskers. Roar peaks here, but no direct injury is shown. Camera gently pushes in to intensify pressure.

Shot 8 connects with the previous shot via short fade-in/fade-out, wide backlight shot reconstructing spatial relationship. Foreground dust blurs vision; background wreckage silhouettes are cut out by cold white backlight. Camera slowly pulls back horizontally.

Shot 9 connects with the previous shot via action-linked hard cut, medium-close push-in as climax. One lion suddenly leaps onto the wreckage of a wrecked vehicle and lets out a high-position roar. The other stops in the dust, lowers its head, then steps aside to yield the center of the ring—establishing dominance without physical knockdown. Dust kicked up under backlight rolls in layers. prompts: Shot 1 serves as the opening shot, beginning with a fade-in into a wide overhead composition. Foreground features mist-like floating sea particles; background shows the exterior facade of the underwater city museum and the entrance to the temporarily converted auditorium. Architectural lines appear slightly hazy due to watercolor blending, guiding the viewer’s focus toward the slowly opening door. A judge fish enters from the lower left of the frame, trailing small bubbles from its tail fin. Cold natural diffused light covers the stone steps outside the museum. The camera slightly tilts down then slowly pushes in.

Shot 2 cuts hard to a medium-close eye-level composition, focusing on the interior of the converted courtroom. Cold overhead lighting presses down from above, creating clear depth between the evidence table and seating. The defendant fish is positioned slightly right of center. Blurred foreground includes the edge of the table and floating documents; blurred background shows the audience seats. The fish stands rigid, fins tightly closed, eyes uneasy, frozen before the evidence table. Gentle currents cause slight fluttering of clothing edges. The camera performs a very subtle lateral pan. Shot 3 cuts hard to a close-up shot from a slightly low-angle side perspective. The prosecutor fish occupies the left foreground, with a floating projection screen in the right background. Cold overhead light creates sharp highlights along its dorsal fin and robe edges. The prosecutor raises its fin to project subway surveillance footage, where a pearl badge is highlighted by a spotlight. Focus quickly shifts from the prosecutor’s action to the glowing lost badge. The camera smoothly pushes in toward the projection surface.

Shot 4 transitions via match cut directly into the projected content, becoming a full-frame overhead view of the subway turnstile replay. Cold cyan-colored turnstile lines are softened in the watercolor style. Foreground shows the turnstile barriers; background features a rush of swimming passenger fish. The suspect fish swiftly passes through the crowd, its tail flicking up a trail of chaotic bubbles. The camera pans horizontally to follow its motion, briefly accelerating as it passes the turnstile, creating a momentary illusion that the evidence is conclusive.

Shot 5 cuts hard back to a medium eye-level shot inside the courtroom, then transitions via picture-in-picture projection to the amusement park ticket booth recording. The defense fish is on the right; a floating screen on the left displays the ticket booth window and timestamp. Cold side lighting outlines its silhouette. It calmly retrieves another recording and points out the time discrepancy. The camera first slightly zooms in on the fish’s fin movements, then gently shifts toward the changing timestamp on the screen, allowing viewers to clearly see the inconsistency with the previous surveillance.

Shot 6 fades into a close-up eye-level shot in the stadium corridor. Blurred foreground railings direct attention to the central witness fish. Mixed lighting includes cold white ceiling lights and diffused seabed light. Wall surfaces reflect subtle water ripples. The witness fish trembles slightly, fins contracted, eyes darting when speaking. An empty space on the right suggests the pressure of cross-examination. The camera slowly pushes in to a semi-close-up. Distant stadium echoes subtly blend into the overall soundscape.

Shot 7 cuts hard to a close-up overhead shot of the evidence table in the courtroom. Composition focuses intensely on the cracked pearl badge and the wet, curled ticket stub placed side by side. Foreground shows the edge of a transparent evidence holder; background blurs the silhouettes of prosecutor and defense. Cold overhead light reveals clear textures on the badge crack and paper fibers. Water stains can be seen slowly spreading along the paper edges. The camera makes a very slow, slight circular movement, visually linking the two pieces of evidence within the same frame.

Shot 8 cuts hard with foreground obstruction into a medium-close confrontation shot. Cold side lighting places prosecutor and defense on opposite sides of the frame, with a compressed perspective channel between them. In the background, layered projections show a display case diagram and alarm trajectory. The composition draws focus to the advancing fin gestures and central display case image. After a brief verbal clash, the truth is reconstructed: the alarm was triggered accidentally at the museum display case, not theft. The camera first rapidly pans left and right to simulate verbal collision, then stabilizes abruptly and gently pushes toward the central diagram at the moment of revelation. Chinese String

Foreground shows still audience silhouettes; background reveals deep-sea shadows moving outside through the hall doors. Cold lighting includes subtle natural reflections. A brief pause follows, then the atmosphere relaxes. The defendant fish slowly loosens its body, and surrounding fish shift from tension to relief. After the gavel strike, the camera slowly pulls back, re-incorporating the temporary courtroom into the museum space.

prompts: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in, a wide eye-level composition showing the full stone tower workshop, foreground featuring a rough stone table, midground with soldering iron, rune circuit board, and clamping fixture, background revealing cold blue moonlight through arched windows and slowly flickering magical runes on the wall. Deep depth of field keeps both environment and tools sharp. Warm firelight illuminates the table edges while cool blue light outlines tool contours. An elderly male stands beside the table, firmly securing the work area and disconnecting power. The camera performs a slight push-in, helping viewers quickly grasp the safety starting point.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view focusing on the stone table surface. Solder wire spool, flux bottle, and tweezers are arranged diagonally, with the rune circuit board blurred in the background as a guide. Firelight remains the key light, with blue rune reflections on metallic edges. The instructor's fingers point to each tool in turn; objects emit subtle pixel shimmer when touched. Chinese voiceover simultaneously names their functions, maintaining a composed tone. The camera performs a short lateral slide, following the hand movement from left to right to complete the inventory.

Shot 3 transitions via hard cut to an extreme close-up from a slightly angled overhead perspective. Focus centers on the iron tip and damp cleaning sponge. Foreground shows the glowing iron tip, background softly blurred to retain flux bottle and stone texture. Warm light creates stable highlights on metal surfaces. The instructor first cleans the iron tip, then gently touches solder to the tip to form an even thin layer. Chinese The camera makes a slight tilt-down motion, pressing details more fully into frame.

Shot 4 continues with a hard cut to a medium-close overhead view using a tutorial-style top-down composition. Stone table edge forms a stable frame, hands centered in the image, wire, wire stripper, and circuit board pads clearly arranged front-to-back. Key light still comes from upper-right warm fire bowl, fill light from left-side blue rune lamp. The instructor first strips the wire to expose neat metal strands, then quickly pre-tins the pad with the iron. Both wire end and pad surface show uniform shiny thin solder layers. Chinese The camera remains stable, only making a minimal push-in to enhance step readability.

Shot 5 cuts via hard cut to a close-up eye-level view. Composition places the rune circuit board in the lower half of the frame, foreground slightly blurred with a short piece of solder wire, midground clearly showing hole positions, background revealing the instructor’s chest leather apron and flickering firelight. A resistor and an LED are picked up one by one, oriented correctly, and inserted into board holes. The moment component leads pass through holes aligns clearly with pixelated copper traces on the board. Chinese The camera performs a slow lateral follow, ensuring finger, component, and hole relationships remain clear.

Shot 6 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up at a slightly upward-angled eye-level view. Pad and component lead occupy the center of frame, shallow depth of field blurring the workshop background into soft pixel blocks. Iron tip enters from the right side, contacting both pad and lead simultaneously. Then solder is fed from the left. Upon heating, solder flows, spreads, and contracts into a full, conical joint. This material transformation is the focal point of this shot. The instructor emphasizes “烙铁同时碰焊盘和引脚”, with sentence timing perfectly aligned to the moment the iron touches. The camera performs a very short push-in, enhancing the credibility of the joint formation detail.

Shot 7 connects via hard cut to a medium eye-level shot beginning a dolly move. Composition smoothly shifts from one side of the board to the other. Foreground occasionally sweeps past tweezers and snips, adding speed layering. Midground continuously locks onto the soldering area. Warm firelight maintains table clarity, blue fill light outlines edges. The instructor completes the other side using the same method, then cleanly clips excess leads with snips. Metal fragments bounce to the edge of the stone table. Movements are fluid and controlled. Chinese voiceover briefly supplements the trimming step.

Shot 8 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up overhead view. Centered are several completed joints. Foreground shows magnifier frame edge, background displays faint rune patterns. Lighting remains consistent, with slightly enhanced highlight reflection on joint surfaces. The instructor gently prods components with tweezers to confirm stability, then checks each joint for fullness, roundness, absence of cold solder or bridging. Joint surfaces display clear light-dark block changes in pixel art style. Chinese Camera nearly static, only making a tiny zoom-in to enhance inspection feel.

Shot 9 connects via a gentle fade-in/fade-out transition, shifting to a close-up eye-level view with rapid push-in. The rune circuit board at the center of the stone table becomes the main subject again. Foreground shows power switch, background reveals the elderly male’s facial outline with satisfied smile. Warm firelight illuminates his wrinkles, cool blue rune light gradually lights up the board in grid pattern. After he turns on the power, runes glow steadily rather than flicker, component operation status clearly visible. In the final half-second, the camera freezes between the glowing circuit board and his smile, forming a complete, coherent, executable tutorial ending.

Foreground features floating clouds and copper bells at eaves; midground shows a wooden tea pavilion suspended over the sea of clouds; background displays layered fairy mountains and a pale blue sky. Cool diffused light envelops the pavilion. One traveler just takes a bite when suddenly chokes, leaning forward, shoulders jerking. The other traveler looks up from the opposite side of the table, noticing the anomaly. The camera slowly pushes forward, focusing attention for the upcoming instruction.

Shot 2 connects via hard cut from the previous shot, close-up, eye-level angle. Composition focuses on the upper body and neck of the choking person, with tea pavilion railings and swirling clouds in the background as minimal backdrop. The subject's face lies on the rule of thirds, throat and hands as visual focal points. Lighting continues with cool soft glow. Cloak and collar flutter slightly due to struggle. The lens performs slight handheld forward movement, intensifying urgency in symptom recognition.

Shot 3 connects via hard cut, extreme close-up, eye-level slightly off-center angle. Foreground blurs the rescuer’s reaching hand; midground clearly captures the moment the rescuer observes facial and throat reactions of the choking person; background remains pavilion pillars and cold mist. Soft backlight from behind and to the side outlines the silhouette. The camera holds still for half a second, then makes a small pan to follow the rescuer into position.

Shot 4 connects via hard cut, medium close-up, eye-level angle. Composition fully includes both individuals from waist up, rescuer’s arms forming clear crossing lines. Background simplified to pavilion railing and sea of clouds, ensuring hand placement is most prominent. Under cool diffused light, the rescuer demonstrates placing fist above navel, wrapping the other hand, then delivering continuous inward and upward thrusts. Movements are distinct and visible—each push shows elbow tightening, back stabilizing, patient’s torso briefly shifting, clothing and belt subtly vibrating with force. Camera performs slight push-in and maintains stable tracking during each thrust, emphasizing standard positioning and motion path.

Shot 5 connects via brief fade transition, overhead shot, full-to-medium composition. Stone platform centered, forming stable geometric structure. Foreground shows scattered snacks and overturned cup; background still reveals pavilion edge and flowing mist. Narratively, it naturally follows loss of responsiveness. Even cool soft lighting persists. The choking person suddenly loses consciousness. The rescuer immediately supports head and upper body, laying them smoothly onto the stone platform. Facial shadows are delicate but not harsh, enhancing the atmosphere of fragility and comfort. prompts: Shot 1 serves as the opening shot, starting with a wide eye-level view. The camera slowly dollies in from the entrance of the museum physics interactive exhibit. Foreground features low-saturation display board edges and semi-transparent signage; background includes softly lined interactive equipment and sparse visitors. The subject, a young man with shounen anime traits, walks into the center of the frame and stops before the protective platform. Composition uses cabinet edges and floor lines to guide the viewer’s gaze toward the sealed transparent sphere on the platform. Shallow depth of field keeps both the character and device sharp while slightly blurring the background crowd. Soft light evenly fills the hall, with gentle reflections on glass surfaces but no glare. the second half lands precisely on the moment his lips curl upward and his finger freezes.

Shot 2 connects to the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up side angle. The camera quickly pans near one side of the protective shield, shifting focus rapidly from the steel ball’s trajectory to the surface of the transparent sphere. Composition places the curved shield surface in the foreground as a natural frame, mid-ground shows the impact point, and background features subdued audience area and gallery light strips. Under consistent neutral tones and soft lighting, sharper highlights appear at the moment of impact. The instant the steel ball strikes the sphere, the transition from intact to crack propagation to full explosion is fully recorded. Fragments of varying sizes eject outward along different arcs. Larger shards initially rush toward the shield before slowing and sliding down, while finer particles briefly shimmer with translucent quality under the lights. Multiple collision trails and fine scratches are clearly visible on the inner surface of the shield. Clothing edges and hair strands subtly flutter due to the subject’s sudden forward lean. The camera pauses briefly at the densest cluster of trajectories, emphasizing “破碎路径” as a key visual element.

Shot 3 continues with another hard cut into the closing segment, using an extreme close-up overhead view with a slow pull-out. Filming starts from the ground safety observation zone. Foreground shows clearly marked landing lines and numbers; focus rests on scattered fragments and several typical arc patterns. Mid-ground features the young man crouching, hand reaching close to the ground without touching the danger boundary. Background includes the base of the protective platform and blurred human silhouettes. Lighting remains soft and diffused, with only minimal cool glass reflections preserved on fragment edges, allowing lines and color blocks in the watercolor style to feel both controlled and dynamic. As the camera slowly pulls back, it re-incorporates the character, ground markings, fragment landing points, and protective platform into a single frame, ultimately freezing on a complete and readable ejection distribution map, concluding with the experiment result clearly observed and displayed.

Warm golden window lights stand out against the cold dark background, emphasizing the observation tower's seaside position, seemingly awaiting something. Candles on both sides create repeating perspective lines leading toward a dark archway ahead. Foreground candles are slightly blurred; stained glass windows in the background tremble slightly under heavy rain. Warm candlelight outlines her figure. Brief flashes of cold blue lightning from outside briefly illuminate the stone walls. She moves cautiously, her cloak hem lifted gently by crosswind. Lantern light flickers on the wall, elongating her shadow. The camera follows her backward along the corridor with slight pan, creating a sense of forward pull toward the unknown.

The character is positioned slightly right and lower in frame, her lantern a warm light point in the rotating space. The observation tower’s inner walls are damp and weathered. Narrow arrow slits let in strong wind, which creates hollow echoing in the tower cavity. She descends steadily, one hand on the wall, one holding the lantern. Her pace shifts from cautious to increasingly drawn forward. The flame tilts sideways in the wind. Water puddles on the edge of the steps reflect faint glimmers. The camera follows from above along the spiral path, then slightly tilts to enhance the sensation of descent.

Composition uses the direction of fish movement to guide the viewer’s gaze toward the office space behind the glass. Cool blue diffused light illuminates window frames and desk edges. The camera slowly pushes forward through gaps in the fish school, establishing the setting of an office submerged in the deep sea yet still operating normally.

The scene transitions. Shot 2 follows with a hard cut, using a medium-wide eye-level perspective from inside the office looking out through the floor-to-ceiling window. Foreground elements include floating data screens and office partitions; midground shows a row of illuminated workstations; in the background, the massive silhouette of the silver-scaled dragon glides slowly overhead through a corridor. Composition places the dragon’s shadow horizontally across the orderly grid of desks, creating strong contrast. Underwater cool lighting maintains tonal consistency, and for the first time, a faint aurora appears at the edge of its scales. The camera performs a slight pan to follow its path.

The scene transitions. Shot 3 cuts sharply to a close-up overhead shot, focusing on keyboards, folders, touchscreens, and continuously rising fine bubbles. Shallow depth of field keeps foreground keycaps sharp while blurring background monitors. Light bands flow along screen edges and plastic-covered documents, adding subtle blue-green reflections to the dominant cool blue palette. Water currents stirred by the dragon cause paper pages to flutter and alter bubble trajectories. The camera executes a short lateral slide with slight push-in. The scene transitions. Shot 4 transitions via a soft dissolve to a close-up upward angle, lifting from behind a desk to face the upper body of the dragon. Composition centers its head and neck as the main focal point, while the ceiling in the background gradually transforms into a polar night dome, replacing scattered light strips with star-like cold lights. Backlighting outlines the silver scales.

The scene transitions. Shot 5 connects with a hard cut to a medium eye-level shot in the meeting room area. Foreground features water ripples reflected on glass walls; midground shows the dragon’s long tail sweeping across the meeting room glass; background reveals projection equipment and floating documents on tables. Composition uses glass reflections to create layered depth. As the tail passes, auroras ripple like ribbons along the glass edges. Under consistent cool blue diffusion, more pronounced blue-green streaks appear.

The scene transitions. Foreground includes small floating items on desks; midground shows the office area progressively covered by blue-green light waves; background features blurred distant waters outside the deep-sea window. Composition uses desk rows and corridors as radial leading lines. Lighting remains consistent, but aurora intensity significantly increases. The dragon spirals forward in the center, and the light wave floods desk edges like a tide. The camera slowly pulls back with slight rotation.

The scene transitions. Shot 7 cuts abruptly to a close-up eye-level shot, capturing one of the dragon’s eyes at extreme proximity. Foreground is softly blurred with scattered bubbles and scattered light points; focus locks onto a circular light curtain reflected within the iris. Shallow depth of field emphasizes the rotating aurora texture in the pupil. A ring of blue-green highlight slides along the pupil’s edge over a cool blue base. The camera remains nearly static, with only minimal push-in, allowing the image to briefly contract after high intensity. When The chant remains ethereal but gains greater penetration.

The scene transitions. Composition uses the dragon’s body to form a strong diagonal, emphasizing spatial movement and performance climax. Cool blue diffusion remains consistent, and auroras reach maximum brightness, erupting simultaneously from scales, tail, and dome. The final note of the chant is stretched, perfectly synchronized with the sudden bloom of light bands.

The scene transitions. Shot 9 transitions via a slow fade-in/fade-out into the closing shot, using a medium rear eye-level view. The dragon hovers silently in front of the floor-to-ceiling window. prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in into a wide eye-level composition. Foreground shows the laid-out yoga mat, mid-ground features a young woman standing at the center of the mat, background includes the window-side training area, dumbbell rack, and resistance bands. Window frame and floor lines form natural leading lines, focusing on the relationship between the subject and the training space. Cool morning light enters from the side-rear, outlining the subject’s silhouette and equipment edges.

Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot to a close-up eye-level view, framing the upper body and abdominal region. Subject is positioned slightly off-center in a third-rule composition, background blurred but retaining window outline. Lighting remains cool natural light with soft fill. She demonstrates proper stance while clearly explaining “脚踩稳，收腹，肩膀放松，吸气准备”.

Shot 3 hard cuts to an extreme close-up eye-level shot, focusing on shoulder-neck and arm range of motion. Background depth of field is shallower, with cool window light creating thin contour lines on skin edges. She begins shoulder-neck circles and arm-opening warm-up, first slowly rotating shoulders, then opening arms outward. Movements are smooth and rhythmically steady. The camera makes small lateral follow movements to keep joint actions centered.

Shot 4 hard cuts to a medium eye-level shot, showing full-body in frame. Foreground retains minimal floor space for depth, background remains clean gym room with cool natural window light. Focus is on hip-knee-ankle coordination. She fully demonstrates squats: hinging hips back, lowering slowly, pausing, then rising upright. Knee trajectory is stable without inward collapse. She emphasizes “下蹲吸气，起身呼气，膝盖跟脚尖方向一致” in Camera slightly tilts down then up, following center-of-mass shift.

Shot 5 connects via smooth transition hard cut to a medium lateral pan shot. Subject moves to mirror area. Mirror in background reflects body side profile, creating dual foreground-background observation. Focus locks on front knee, toe direction, and trunk stability. Cool lighting remains consistent, with only soft reflection at mirror edge. She steps forward into lunge, bending front and back legs sequentially before returning to standing. Movement repeats once to reinforce learning. Camera laterally follows, showing both front and side posture.

Shot 6 transitions via quick downward cut to an overhead shot. Viewpoint directly above the mat. Mat edges and hand-elbow positions form clear geometric composition. Subject’s body occupies vertical axis. Focus precisely on elbow-shoulder-back alignment. Natural light from one side casts diagonal shadows on mat, revealing true texture. She lowers into plank position: elbows down, shoulders aligned, core engaged, body straight from head to heels. Camera maintains slight pitch adjustment to keep key support points visible.

Shot 7 hard cuts to a close-up low-angle shot from front-side. Shallow depth of field blurs background equipment. Focus follows knee advancement and flat back posture. Cool lighting unchanged, but ground reflects subtle bright strip. She begins slow mountain climbers, alternating legs forward, maintaining steady pace. Shoulders remain still, back does not sag. She reminds “慢一点也没关系，腰背不要塌”. Camera performs short push-pull movements to highlight core engagement and control.

Shot 8 connects via soft fade cut to a medium-wide eye-level shot. Frame pulls back, subject lying supine on mat. Foreground shows raised knees and pelvis, background still reveals window-side training area. Spatial continuity is clear. Focus shifts from glute bridge peak to posterior chain stretch. Cool natural light forms clean bright stripes on floor. She completes one standard glute bridge: lifts pelvis, tightens glutes, pauses, then lowers. Then smoothly transitions into leg hug and hamstring stretch. Movement flow is fluid. She gives brief cue “抬起时夹紧臀部，放下后接腿后侧拉伸”. Camera first slightly pulls back, then stabilizes, making full transition visible. Exhalation synchronizes strictly with lowering and stretching phases.

Shot 9 fades in to conclude with a close-up eye-level shot by the window. Composition focuses on face, neck, and subtly rising chest. Background is blurred window frame and soft cool daylight. Shallow depth of field makes facial expression the sole focus. Key light remains natural side light, with soft fill preserving skin texture realism. She returns to window, gently places hands, slowly inhales then exhales. Expression is focused and encouraging.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. The subject is seated in front of a vanity mirror, with slightly blurred makeup brushes and skincare bottles in the foreground. The focus is on her clear, bare face and its reflection in the mirror. The background features warm-toned home decor and desk organization, with soft lighting spreading from the side-front, revealing natural skin texture. She gently raises her hand to indicate her facial condition, then points to the products on the table, clearly mouthing “今天做一个清透通勤妆，保留自然感”. The camera slowly pushes in, establishing the tutorial's goal and initial state.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up overhead view with a slight first-person perspective, creating a continuous composition from the tabletop to the face. Focus initially lands on her fingers unscrewing the cap of a moisturizer, then follows to her cheeks and forehead. Skincare products on the table form leading lines, with shallow depth of field emphasizing the texture of lotion and primer. She presses the moisturizer into her palm and gently spreads it across her face, then dots primer onto her cheeks, forehead, and chin, narrating in Chinese “先保湿，再薄上一层隔离让后续更服帖”. The The camera slightly tilts down and pans to follow her hand.

Shot 3 enters with a hard cut matching the action, shifting to a close-up facial detail, using a near-eye-level shot. A sponge is held in the foreground, while the mirror background is softly blurred. Focus tightly follows the foundation application from the bridge of the nose to the cheeks. Under consistent warm lighting, foundation is dotted onto the face and evenly patted out with the sponge in rhythmic motions. Localized skin tone gradually unifies, surface becomes smoother while retaining natural texture. The camera gently pushes in and slightly pans right to emphasize the transition from partial to full-face coverage.

Shot 4 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a tighter close-up of the under-eye and nostril area, framed in a slight high-angle close-up composition. The center of the frame focuses on the alternating motion between the concealer brush and fingertip, while the background softens into warm, blurred color blocks. She precisely dabs concealer onto the inner corners of the dark circles and both sides of the nostrils, then gently blends it using a small brush and fingertip. The dullness gradually brightens and the redness softens visibly. The camera remains nearly static, with only a minimal push-in to emphasize fine details.

Shot 5 transitions via a hard cut into eyebrow tutorial, using a medium close-up at a slightly angled eye-level view. The mirror image and real person form a dual-layer composition, focus locked on the eyebrow shape and the eyebrow pencil in hand.

It begins with a close-up overhead view capturing the eyeshadow palette and brush picking up pigment, then smoothly transitions to a frontal close-up of the eyes. She blends light brown shadow into the crease, applies a deeper shade at the outer corner, carefully lines along the base of the lashes, and finally curls her lashes. The eye's definition becomes progressively more vivid, with lashes lifting into a graceful curve. The camera initially moves forward slightly, pauses briefly, then subtly tilts upward following the curling motion, enhancing the sense of sequential progression.

Shot 7 transitions from the previous shot with a soft dissolve into cheek enhancement, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. Composition balances both cheeks symmetrically, with a highlighter palette below forming a secondary guide. In the same soft warm light, she lightly sweeps blush on the outer apples of the cheeks, then uses a small brush to add highlight to the bridge of the nose and cheekbones. Her complexion visibly becomes softer and more radiant, with controlled natural glow on the skin surface.

Shot 8 cuts sharply from the previous shot into a close-up of the lips, using an eye-level extreme close-up. Background maintains consistent warm tone and shallow depth of field. The camera slightly pushes in, then stabilizes gently, highlighting the final step before completion.

Shot 9 concludes with a soft dissolve from the previous shot, using a medium shot at eye-level with a slight mirror-facing composition. On the left, either a small inset of her original bare face or a head turn creates a before-and-after comparison; on the right, the completed makeup is shown directly. Focus is on the overall clear, unified finish and facial expression change. Background remains the same vanity area, warm lighting stable, avoiding stylistic jumps. The soft The camera first slightly pulls back to establish the full view, then gently pushes back to freeze-frame on the before-and-after contrast, forming a complete narrative loop.
